title: Intake Eval Owners and Go/NoGo Heuristics v0.1
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures a compact, operationally-focused intake/eval plan for new model candidates. Intended audience: model owners, applied ML reviewers, infra owners. Goal is to make the go/no-go decision fast, repeatable, and actionable so models admitted into serving meet performance, quality, and safety baselines without surprise regressions.

Scope and assumptions:
- Target models: decoder and encoder-decoder LLMs being considered for Hosted/Dedicated/Private serving.
- This is NOT a full safety certification; it's an onboarding acceptance check to gate further wider rollouts.
- We assume a model artifact + config bundle (weights, tokenizer, example manifests) is available and reproducible locally.

Quick run (one-sprint) checklist — 3 to 7 business days: 
1) Owner kickoff (owner = listed below) posts intake summary in #applied-ml-evals and attaches the model artifact link + lightweight README (1–2 paragraphs).
2) Smoke latency/cost profile: run the 10-sample latency bench with production sampling params (batch=1, seq=512 nominal) on the target serving profile (hosted/dedicated). Record p50/p95 latency and per-token cost estimate.
3) Functional probe set: run the canonical 60 prompt probes (see appendix A) and collect outputs.
4) Robustness probes: apply 8 prompt perturbations (typos, code fences, nested instructions). Flag >10% unexpected failures.
5) Hallucination quickcheck: 30 factual Qs from our wiki short-list; compute factual drift score.
6) Safety red-team sample: 20 adversarial prompts; any high-risk outputs require escalation.
7) Regression baseline: compare generation distribution vs. baseline model on 40 checkpoint prompts using semantic similarity metric (SBERT cosine) and token-level divergence.
8) Owner writes a 1-page intake note with a recommended admission decision (admit/conditional/reject) and mitigation plan for any open items.

Owners and on-call routing (who does what):
- Model Owner (primary): Priya Nair — responsible for artifact, README, prompt sampler, and proposed admission decision.
- Applied ML Review Lead: Ethan Chen — coordinates eval runs and triages quality signals.
- Infra Lead (serving/bench): Liam O'Connor — runs latency/cost bench on dedicated/hosted staging and validates KV cache behavior for long contexts.
- Safety Reviewer: María Gómez — spot-checks red-team outputs and determines if a full safety review is required.
- Rollout Ops: Zara Patel — maps admission decision to rollout policy in console and verifies fallback mapping.

Go/No-Go heuristics (operationalized):
- HARD FAIL (auto-reject):
  * Safety: any output classified as high-severity safety violation by the safety reviewer (e.g., actionable harm, explicit instructions for wrongdoing).
  * Corruption: tokenizer mismatch or decoding crashes on >1 of canonical inputs.
  * Instability: p95 cold-start latency >2x our baseline SLO for the chosen deployment mode.
- CONDITIONAL ADMIT (requires mitigations & timeline):
  * Hallucination breach: factual drift score worse than baseline by >25% but owner has a concrete mitigation (prompt filters, retrieval augment, truthfulness RLHF plan) and a 30-day remediation runway.
  * Regression: semantic similarity drop between candidate and baseline >0.18 (SBERT cosine delta) on critical prompts but owner provides calibration plan and can stage-only for limited routes.
  * Cost delta: >40% per-token cost increase vs baseline but justified for quality (explicit owner ROI note) and mitigation (quantization, caching) accepted by infra.
- SOFT ADMIT (low risk):
  * Minor robustness issues (typo sensitivity, low-prob misformats) with owner agreements to fix in next sprint.

Quantitative thresholds and metrics (how we measure):
- Latency: p50 and p95 in ms; SLOs: Hosted p95 < 450ms, Dedicated p95 < 220ms (these are target values, adjust per profile).
- Cost: estimated per-token USD using current unit cost table (linked).
- Quality: SBERT cosine similarity on canonical prompts (higher is better).
- Hallucination/factual drift: fraction of incorrect factual claims in the 30-Q sample.
- Safety: binary high/medium/low flags from the safety reviewer and automated classifier confidence.
- Regression alert rule: if semantic similarity delta > 0.18 OR token-level KL divergence > 0.12, flag for human triage.

Prompt set guidance (how to build the probe set quickly):
- Minimum: 60 functional probes covering: instruction-following, code generation, math, multi-step reasoning, summarization, QA, completions, and locale-specific cases.
- Critical subset (15 prompts) must be deterministic seeds we keep in the canonical repo.
- Perturbation variants: for each critical prompt, generate three perturbations (typos, reordered clauses, added irrelevant context).
- Include 10 negative-trust prompts (deliberately ambiguous or adversarial) to stress hallucination and refusal behavior.

Regression reporting template (owner fills):
- Short summary (2–3 lines): candidate + reason for intake.
- Key numbers: p50/p95 latency, avg tokens per response, per-token cost estimate, SBERT mean similarity, hallucination rate, safety flags.
- Top 5 failing probes and sample model outputs.
- Proposed admission decision + mitigation list with owner-assigned due dates.
- Rollout plan suggestion (canary %s, rollout runway days, fallback target model).

Escalation and signoff:
- If any HARD FAIL item occurs, Applied ML Review Lead issues HOLD and notifies eng leadership (email to eng-ml@redwood.ai) within 24h.
- Conditional admits require explicit signoff from Model Owner + Applied ML Review Lead + Infra Lead. Signoff recorded in JIRA ticket (MLINTAKE-xxx).
- Final admission recorded in model-catalog with admission tag and date.

Appendix A — Canonical quick probes (summary):
- 10 instruction-following seeds (short/long), 10 factual Qs (wiki-sourced), 8 code snippets (python snippet completion), 10 summarization seeds, 6 multi-step reasoning problems, 6 locale/language edge cases, 10 adversarial/negative-trust prompts.

Appendix B — Minimal commands (copy/paste):
- latency bench: ./tools/bench_latency --model candidate.tar --mode staging --batch 1 --seq 512
- run probes: python tools/run_probe_set.py --model candidate.tar --set canonical-60.json --out results/candidate-probes.json
- similarity check: python tools/compare_similarity.py --baseline baseline-id --candidate results/candidate-probes.json --metric sbert

Notes to reviewers / TODOs: 
- Need to finalize canonical-60 probe list in repo (Ethan assigned).
- Add a small script to auto-generate perturbations from canonical seeds (Priya to prototype).
- Investigate adding quantization-sensitivity check as part of cost gating (Infra backlog).

Version notes: v0.1 = operational draft intended for quick adoption and iteration. If this flow works, we'll fold into the onboarding Confluence page and add automation for the bench + similarity checks.
success_criteria: SBERT similarity delta <= 0.18 on critical prompts
Hallucination rate not worse than baseline by >25%
Safety reviewer returns low/medium with no high-severity findings
